page.overview:
What is Mato Mato no Mi?

The Mato Mato no Mi is a Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that makes the user capable of aiming at whichever "target" he decides upon from any location and at any time with anything at ease. It was eaten by Flying Pirates captain Vander Decken IX.

Due to Decken telling others that this power is a "curse", it has also been referred to as the .

This fruit makes the user capable of aiming at whoever they touch with their hands. The user can also memorize as many targets with as many hands as he has (in Vander Decken IX's case, two). After the user's hand is imprinted with the memory of the target, the user is able to target the person from any location and at any time with anything at ease, regardless of whether or not they are aware of the target's actual location. Even if the targets move away from their current locations, the thrown objects will pursue them, immediately changing their trajectory in order to chase their targets. Also, if the target the user has chosen happens to be anywhere near them, the thrown projectile will actually even swerve back in a manner not unlike to a boomerang coming back to its thrower. In addition, while the user is affected by the sea water, the objects used to target the recipient(s) can still travel underwater, without the sea affecting or decreasing the intended function.

The user can send any kind of object towards a marked target, no matter how big or small it is. Decken was able to throw the Noah, a ship nearly equal to the size of Fish-Man Island, towards Shirahoshi in an effort to destroy her along with the entire island. Furthermore, as shown with Noah, the user does not even need to actually throw an object for it to fly towards the target. All Decken had to do was touch the giant ship with a memorized hand and the ship itself rose off the sea bed without any assistance, aimed towards Shirahoshi. The user can also turn living organisms as projectiles, as Decken threw a large group of human pirates towards Shirahoshi by touching each one of them. Outside of combat, the power can serve as a sort of homing device to find the target's location. Decken used this idea to find Shirahoshi when he realized she was not in the tower. He threw a large piece of coral and then jumped on it, riding it to Shirahoshi's location.
